country.name: Paraguay
country.tagline: Jesuit mission vines, German settlers and a handful of hectares in the humid hills of Guairá.

stats.note: About 150 ha of grapes, almost all table grapes (ABC Color, 2016); wine output tiny and unrecorded by OIV.

country.overview:
Paraguay sits squarely in the humid subtropics, with hot summers and heavy rain, and has never been a natural home for the vine. Its wine history comes in three short chapters. In the Jesuit mission period, from the late 16th century, missionaries planted European grapes in the *reducciones* of the south-east to make wine for Mass, as part of self-sufficient Guaraní communities. After independence in the early 19th century, viticulture faded as Paraguayans turned to yerba mate and beer, and sacramental wine was imported.

The modern thread is German. In the early 20th century immigrant families planted vines in the hills of Guairá department; Colonia Independencia, founded in 1919 to 1920 at the foot of the Ybytyruzú range, became the centre of Paraguayan grape growing, mostly for table grapes and fruit wine, and holds a harvest festival each year. A 2016 estimate put the national vineyard at about 150 ha, with only a small share used for wine and a single known commercial winery in Colonia Independencia making a few thousand litres of Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon. Paraguay had no active wine exports as of 2024.

history.title: Jesuit mission vines
history.text: Jesuit missionaries plant vines in the Guaraní reducciones of south-eastern Paraguay for sacramental wine, until the order's expulsion in 1767.

history.title: Wine fades
history.text: After independence, viticulture declines as yerba mate and beer dominate and Mass wine is imported.

history.title: Carlos Voigt's vineyard
history.text: Carlos Voigt, a grower of German heritage, begins growing grapes in Guairá, marking the rebirth of Paraguayan viticulture.

history.title: Colonia Independencia
history.text: The agricultural colony of Independencia is founded in Guairá; German and Paraguayan families make it the centre of the country's grape growing.

country.classification: Paraguay has no wine appellation system or specific wine regulation comparable to its neighbours; wine is governed by general food and Mercosur rules.
country.climate_soils: Humid subtropical climate with abundant rain (often 1,300 to 1,700 mm) and hot summers; the slightly higher, cooler hills of Guairá around the Ybytyruzú range are the only area with a grape-growing tradition.

grapes.name: American and hybrid table grapes
grapes.note: Most of the small vineyard area grows table grapes.

grapes.name: Riesling, Cabernet Sauvignon
grapes.note: Grown in tiny quantities by artisanal producers in Colonia Independencia.

sources.title: ABC Color, Analizarán potencial vitivinícola del país (2016)

sites.name: Colonia Independencia
sites.text: A farming town in Guairá department, founded in 1919 to 1920 at the foot of the Ybytyruzú hills, settled in part by German families. It is the centre of Paraguay's small grape-growing tradition and hosts an annual grape and wine festival; a 2016 report counted a single commercial winery here producing about 1,200 litres a year.
